name: @yordan/design-system
description: AI-ready, repo-first design system for the blueprint portfolio. Source of truth: tokens/tokens.json + components/*/spec.md + css/components.css. See README.md.
//: `private: true` and no `publishConfig`: this is consumed by `file:`, never from a registry. `version` is still real — scripts/contract-diff.mjs enforces it against the committed contract in RELEASED.json, so a consumer pinning a range gets a semver promise a publish step would otherwise have to make. `exports` is the same statement the boundary gate makes: dist/ and css/ are published, everything else here is private, and a subpath not listed below is unreachable rather than merely undocumented. `assets/` is in `files` and NOT in `exports` on purpose — avatar.svg is fetched by URL from markup, never resolved as a module.
//exports: TWENTY-FOUR subpaths. It was six until phase R2a, which added the Tailwind + React tier: tokens.tailwind.css binds Tailwind v4's @theme namespaces to the custom properties tokens.css already defines, and ./react/<id> is one generated, typed component per definition. keyframes.css is R4's and is the one entry that is not a token file or a component: an animation's name is a global CSS identifier and a class attribute cannot hold an at-rule, so the @keyframes every definition declares ship as a stylesheet the consumer imports beside tokens.css. It grows by one for every block R4 stops hand-authoring, which contract-diff.mjs classifies as additive — so the count here and the version move together or the semver gate goes red. They are ENUMERATED rather than a `./react/*` wildcard for the same reason the first six are: a subpath that is not listed is unreachable, and a wildcard would publish whatever happens to land in the directory. The React entries resolve to .tsx SOURCE — a consumer transpiles them (Next: transpilePackages) and brings class-variance-authority and react itself; this package still declares no dependencies.

scripts.//emit: STARTED AS THE R1 PILOT, now the R4 migration. Every id in PILOT (scripts/emit-css.mjs) has its appearance authored as data in components/<id>/definition.json, and its block in css/components.css is a GENERATED region rendered from it. `emit:css` writes them; `build.mjs --check` re-renders them in memory and byte-compares, so a hand-edit inside a region fails the build. It runs first in `build` for the obvious reason — the check that follows would otherwise be comparing against a stale file. It is deliberately NOT a step of the ROOT `npm run build`: see the header of scripts/emit-css.mjs.
scripts.build: node scripts/emit-css.mjs && node scripts/build.mjs && node scripts/build.mjs --check
scripts.//test: The story gates build storybook-static when it is stale, serve it on an ephemeral port and drive @storybook/test-runner against it — no dev server, and no http-server/wait-on/concurrently. test:a11y:pages serves the REPO ROOT instead and runs axe over the four shipped pages in both themes with no exemptions — it exists because five matrix stories exempt the document-scope landmark rules, so the single-banner assertion lives there and nowhere else (see scripts/page-a11y.mjs). CI needs `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` first. NONE of these joins the root `npm run check`: that gate is offline, browser-free and dependency-light, and all three need Chromium. test:visual is REPORT-ONLY until 2026-09-01 — see .storybook/test-runner.cjs.
